Hi Logan —

We're moving into our renewal conversation with procurement and our security team asked for a short plan on how Redwood will support NexTrend's SOC2 re-attestation. Two specific asks from legal/security:

1) A defined audit evidence handoff process (who will push logs, format, S3/transfer window).
2) Confirmation of the retention window for audit logs during the attestation period and whether Redwood can temporarily increase retention/ingest bandwidth for the audit (we may need burst capacity for a 10-day sampling).

We're also evaluating a potential 20% seat uplift during the renewal if Redwood can guarantee a temporary retention increase and a simple contract amendment to extend the log retention SLA.

Can you share a checklist and a rough cost delta for a provisional seat increase + temporary ingest/retention bump?

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can support a temporary retention uplift and a burst during the attestation sampling window. I put together an evidence checklist and a proposed minimal amendment to the renewal to cover the temporary retention and provisional seats. Please see the attached checklist and the log shipping spec.

Highlights:
- Evidence handoff: we can provide pre-signed S3 exports (CSV + gzipped logs) or share via secure SFTP. Typical SLA for delivery: 3 business days from request.
- Retention: default is 30 days; we can offer a 90-day retention for the attestation window (90-day temporary uplift).
- Burst capacity: we can provision additional ingestion throughput for up to 14 days. We'll need a heads-up 7 calendar days before the window.
- Seats: provisional uplift (temporary increase) can be billed pro-rata for the amendment period; for renewal we can roll it into the committed seats with a 12-month term at a discounted rate.

Estimated commercial impact (very rough): a 20% seat uplift + 14-day ingestion burst = ~USD 6,200 one-time + prorated monthly delta if folded into committed seats. We can firm numbers after procurement confirms target seat count and exact dates.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred evidence delivery (S3 vs SFTP) and tentative audit window dates.
2) We send a short amendment draft (DocuSign) + formal estimate.
3) Kickoff call with Engineering/Marissa to map log retention and exports.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_evidence_checklist_v2.xlsx, log-shipping-spec.pdf

Best,

Hi all —

Adding a few technical constraints so procurement can plan:

- Export format: we typically provide events in newline-delimited JSON and an accompanying manifest (timestamp range, shard id). If NexTrend needs CSV we can map the most common fields but that increases processing time (we estimate 1-2 business days extra).
- Retention timeline: immediate retention increase to 90 days will require a short data migration (hot tier -> warm tier) and could add ~12% to storage costs for the uplift period.
- Burst: to ensure no ingestion drops, we recommend scheduling the 14-day window with a 7-day warm-up (smaller ramp) — ops needs at least 72 hours notice to apply kernel-level batching adjustments on GPU inference pipelines if you plan to run replays/backfills.
- Access & audit: we can provide a time-limited IAM role with read-only access to the evidence bucket and a log manifest. We will also include SHA256 checksums for parity.

I've left notes in our shared folder (link below) with the specific S3 key patterns and a sample manifest. For the amendment we should capture: start/end dates for retention uplift, whether you want pre-signed URLs or SFTP drops, and whether the provisional seats are temporary or permanent on renewal.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-soc2-evidence
